sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Frankfort, KY?
sections.html:
Frankfort sellers choose among an agent listing, a private sale and a cash offer, and the city adds rules that most Kentucky towns do not have: a rental inspection before any new tenant moves in, short-term rental caps in the historic districts, and floodplain permits along the Kentucky River. Frankfort is the state capital and the seat of Franklin County, with 28,602 residents in the 2020 census and an estimated 28,657 on July 1, 2025.

That is the slowest growth of the four cities in this group, only 0.2% above the 2020 estimates base. A flat population, a large public-sector workforce and a river that has flooded the city more than once all shape how houses here sell.

sections.h2: How does the Frankfort housing market compare?
sections.html:
Frankfort has the lowest median home value and the lowest median household income among the four cities, and its poverty rate is the highest. Renters outnumber owners slightly.

With 2.11 people per household, Frankfort has the smallest households of the group, and retail sales of $20,655 per person in 2022 were the lowest too. Public administration employed 28% of the workforce in 2016, with manufacturing at just over 12%.

sections.h2: Where is Frankfort and what shapes its neighborhoods?
sections.html:
The Kentucky River makes an S-turn through the middle of Frankfort, which creates four parts of town: Downtown and South Frankfort face each other across the river, the small Bellepoint neighborhood sits on the west bank north of Benson Creek, and the suburban West Side and East Side spread out on either side of the valley. Five bridges cross the river downtown.

The site began as a river crossing called Frank's Ford. The Virginia legislature designated 100 acres as the town in 1786, and after Kentucky became a state in 1792 commissioners chose Frankfort as the capital. South Frankfort was annexed on January 3, 1850. Major landmarks include the State Capitol, the Old State Capitol, Liberty Hall and the Buffalo Trace Distillery, with Castle and Key and Three Boys Farm as the other distilleries.

Frankfort has a humid subtropical climate with four seasons. NOAA normals from the airport show about 47 inches of precipitation a year on 138 days, with a record high of 103 degrees in summer and a record low of minus 21 in February, so roofs, gutters and basements get a real workout.

Interstate 64 runs beside the city and Interstate 75 is nearby, with U.S. 60, 460, 127 and 421 crossing it. Commercial flights leave from Blue Grass Airport in Lexington, since Frankfort's Capital City Airport handles general and military aviation.

sections.h2: How does flooding affect selling a house in Frankfort?
sections.html:
The river flooded the city many times, with the highest recorded floods in 1937 and 1978. A levee on the North Frankfort side was finished in 1969 and a floodwall protects South Frankfort. Construction or remodeling inside the floodplain goes through extra review.

  • The Planning and Community Development department runs the flood damage prevention ordinance.
  • Building in the floodplain needs a local Floodplain Development Permit, plus a stream permit from the state Division of Water where one applies.
  • Reviewers use Flood Elevation Certificates signed by a licensed surveyor, engineer or architect.
  • The city says its Community Rating System status saves property owners 10% on flood insurance premiums.

If your house sits near the river, ask Planning and Community Development whether an elevation certificate is on file for the address, and keep any flood insurance paperwork together for the sale.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve Frankfort homes?
sections.html:
Two public districts cover the city. Frankfort Independent Schools serves the downtown neighborhoods, including Downtown, South Frankfort, Bellepoint and Tanglewood, and runs Second Street School, Frankfort High School and an early learning academy. Franklin County Public Schools serves the rest of the city and the county, including Franklin County High School and Western Hills High School.

The split matters for tax as well as schools: the city's Finance Office bills the Frankfort Independent Schools tax along with the city tax. Kentucky State University, a public historically black university and 1890 land-grant institution, sits within the city limits.

sections.h2: How are property taxes billed and paid in Frankfort?
sections.html:
Frankfort property owners deal with two collectors. The city's Finance Office bills the city tax and the Frankfort Independent Schools tax, and the Franklin County Sheriff's Office, at 974 River Bend Road, publishes the county tax bills. The city says values are set by the Franklin County PVA at 100% of fair market value as of January 1.

  • City taxes are available by November 1 and due by December 31.
  • Payments received before November 30 earn a 2% discount.
  • Payments received or postmarked after the due date carry a 10% penalty plus interest.
  • The Finance Office takes questions at 502-875-8500, and bills can be searched and paid online.

Mortgage escrow accounts pay from the bill the servicer receives, so give your lender the tax bill promptly. Address changes go through the Franklin County PVA.

sections.h2: What do landlords and sellers need to know about Frankfort's rental inspection?
sections.html:
Frankfort requires a rental inspection before any new tenant takes possession, however long the previous tenant stayed. The standard fee is $20, and it rises to $100 when a unit has no current inspection. Inspections are usually scheduled the next day, excluding weekends and holidays, and the owner or the owner's agent must be present.

The city does not enforce Kentucky's landlord and tenant act, but its staff will help with health and safety problems that were not present before occupancy or that went uncorrected. Planning and Building answers at 502-352-2094. Short-term rentals sit under separate rules adopted by ordinance in December 2024:

  • An annual $250 license fee for every short-term rental unit.
  • Non-owner-occupied rentals are conditional uses in the Special Capital and Special Historic districts, capped at 5% of dwelling units in the first and 8 rentals in the second.
  • A $100 first citation, then $25 for each further day, and license revocation if the violation continues.

If your house has been a rental or a short-term rental, keep the inspection and registration paperwork together for the sale.

sections.h2: What does a Frankfort seller pay at closing?
sections.html: Under KRS 142.050 the seller owes fifty cents per $500 of value, so a house valued at the Census median of $183,700 owes about $184 in transfer tax, collected by the county clerk when the deed is recorded. Add the mortgage payoff, any lien release and the seller's share of the year's property tax. Agent fees apply only if you list with one, and repair costs fall on whoever agrees to take them on in the contract.

faqs.q: Does Frankfort have its own property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's Finance Office collects the city tax and the Frankfort Independent Schools tax, while the Franklin County Sheriff collects the county bills. Check your bill for the district, or call 502-875-8500.

faqs.q: When is the city of Frankfort's property tax due?
faqs.a: The bills are available by November 1 and due by December 31, and payments received before November 30 get a 2% discount. After the due date a 10% penalty plus interest applies.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental inspection to rent out a Frankfort house?
faqs.a: Yes. A rental inspection is required before any new tenant takes possession, and the fee is $20, or $100 if the unit has no current inspection. Call Planning and Building at 502-352-2094 to schedule it.

faqs.q: Can I run a short-term rental in Frankfort?
faqs.a: Yes, with limits. Each unit pays a $250 annual license fee, and non-owner-occupied rentals in the Special Capital and Special Historic districts are conditional uses with caps. Owner-occupied rentals must meet the ordinance's standards for stay length, occupancy and parking.

faqs.q: Is a Frankfort house in a flood zone harder to sell?
faqs.a: Floodplain location changes what you can build or remodel, because construction there needs a local Floodplain Development Permit and elevation certificate review. Ask Planning and Community Development whether a certificate is on file for your address.
